```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"These crises have been eye-openers for some and reminders of what government can and should do, because reasserting a strong government role runs against the grain of 30 years of economic thinking dominated by the Right.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Alienation from government has become a self-reinforcing dynamic.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The incessant attack on means-tested programs for the poor has led many white working- and middle-class people to forget that only progressive taxation, state regulation, and public provision can insure them the opportunity to hold a well-paying union job or afford an adequate retirement and college opportunities for their children.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Progressive taxation, state regulation, and public provision can insure white working- and middle-class people the opportunity to hold a well-paying union job or afford an adequate retirement and college opportunities for their children.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"With regulatory oversight and enforcement crippled and with state and local governments stripped of the capacity to provide seamless provision of emergency and social services, government’s failure to respond effectively to community needs or to major crises has reinforced the business-friendly mantra that government is the source of the problem.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
